correctness.rationale: Independently derived the Sherman–Morrison formula for V_t^{-1} with denominator 1+t s>0 because V^{-1}, u and w are nonnegative; hence invertibility is unconditional for t>=0 but inverse positivity requires the stated exact entrywise inequality. Multiplication gives V_t^{-1}u=V^{-1}u/(1+ts). Since F_tV_t^{-1} is nonnegative rank at most one on admissible t, its spectral radius equals (f+tw)^T V_t^{-1}u=(R0+ts)/(1+ts), proving contraction without crossing. A fresh rational 2x2 regular example with V=[[3,-1],[-1,1]], u=(1,1), f=(2,1), w=(1,0), t=1/5 gives R0=4, s=1, Rt=7/2 and Vt^{-1}=[[5/12,5/12],[1/3,4/3]]>=0. For the Johnston–Cupons source formulas, both threshold differences share numerator AD−B(C+D) and the ratio is (C+D)/(C+2D), between 1/2 and 1 for C,D>0. No finite sample is used as proof.

final_claim: For a regular rank-one splitting \(J=F-V\), \(F=uf^{\mathsf T}\ge0\), under the aligned transfer \(F_t=u(f+tw)^{\mathsf T}\), \(V_t=V+tuw^{\mathsf T}\) for nonnegative \(u,f,w\) and \(t\ge0\), the transfer is regular exactly when its explicitly given Sherman–Morrison inverse is entrywise nonnegative. On admissible transfers, \(R_t-1=(R_0-1)/(1+ts)\), \(s=w^{\mathsf T}V^{-1}u\ge0\), so strict movement toward but not across the threshold 1 occurs for \(s,t>0\); the cited example also satisfies an explicit contraction relation between its two source-displayed reproduction numbers.
limitations: Only finite-dimensional rank-one F and aligned nonnegative transfers, with post-transfer inverse positivity explicitly required.
No claim for unaligned/higher-rank updates or a uniquely meaningful biological reproduction number.
The source Example 3.12 scalar identity is a known-formula corollary and not independently claimed novel.
